title: Why Barnes Made the Triangular Bandage
topic: Why the American Civil War surgeon Joseph K. Barnes introduced the “triangular bandage” (to simplify field dressing of wounds)

lines: A Union surgeon flings a cloth triangle over a bleeding arm, eyes fierce.
Fellow medics laugh, muttering that a rag cannot stop a cannon‑shot wound.
Barnes storms the battlefield, smoke curling around him.
He pulls a right‑angled piece of cloth from his satchel.
You see, it feels like folding a napkin into a quick sling when dinner is late.
Barnes adopts the triangular cloth so a medic can wrap, tie, and support a wound in three swift moves.
The fold saves minutes and cuts the chance of a tangled dressing.
That same triangle later became the Scout’s neckerchief, born on Civil War fields.

claims.claim: Joseph K. Barnes served as Surgeon General of the United States Army during the Civil War.
A triangular bandage is a piece of cloth cut into a right‑angled triangle, used as a sling or wound dressing.
